source.title: Understanding and Rectifying Safety Perception Distortion in VLMs
source.authors: Xiaohan Zou; Jian Kang; G. Kesidis; Lu Lin

page_placements.theme: Cross-modality: text-derived refusal direction applied to image, video, audio and VLA inputs

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means safety direction and removes its projection from a modality-induced activation shift, then measures safety behavior. This is a conceptual test of the direction’s role, not the original’s global, all-layer-and-position ablation or addition.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports probe accuracies for choosing and analyzing safety representations; those are included only as findings about safety perception, not refusal behavior. Values used to select calibration layers are not separately recorded. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study works in a new setting: vision-language models (VLMs). It derives a text-only harmful-vs-benign difference-in-means direction. It shows that visual inputs shift activations along that direction toward the benign side, and that this alignment tracks jailbreak success (Fig. 6). Removing that shift component at middle-to-late layers restores refusal (Tables 1, 3). This bears on V1, since moving activations along the direction changes refusal, and on V3, since the attacks act by suppressing the direction. It is not the original's global ablation or addition.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Visual input shifts activations toward a 'safer' region along a safety direction, degrading VLM safety. Removing that component (ShiftDC) restores safety alignment without hurting visual utility.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful/benign text-only difference-in-means safety direction, but subtracts its projection from an image-versus-caption modality shift at selected layers and the last-token activation. It does not project the direction out globally at every position, nor add the direction to induce refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: Calibration layer range matters: beginning at the first layer is reported as poorest, middle-layer starts give the lowest ASR, and calibrating only the last 10 layers gives high ASR.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear safety probes separate text-only inputs (~90%) but not image-text inputs (~65%). A text-trained probe labels most VL inputs safe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a visual modality reduces linear separability of harmful vs. benign inputs along text-derived safety features.

fits_no_version.finding: A direction computed on text-only inputs works as an intervention anchor for image-text inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal/safety direction transfers across input modality (text to vision-language).

record.problems: The reported ASR uses predefined rejection keywords as a rule-based proxy for harmful responses. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The study evaluates VLMs and a selective modality-shift correction, not global direction ablation on chat-only models.
record.rows_left_out: Per-scenario MM-SafetyBench ASRs in Tables 2 and 6-9 were not extracted; the model-by-image-type aggregate ASRs in Table 1 are retained instead. The full scenario tables contain more separate conditions than the 60-row limit permits. Table 5 benign misclassification changes and Figure 8 safety-classifier results are not refusal or harmful-response measures, so they are not rows for the listed versions.

untested.parts: Global all-layer, all-position ablation in text-only chat models; adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal; the effect on refusal of harmless text prompts.
Training against the ablation to add robustness; non-visual (text) jailbreaks.

missing.what: Text-only ASR column, the backbone baseline that ShiftDC matches or beats (e.g. LLaVA 49.2 vs 38.0/39.7/43.6)
Defensive prompts shift activations toward the unsafe side of the direction (negative cosine across layers), linked to over-refusal of benign inputs
Per-scenario ASR showing small gains on scenarios 08 and 10–13 versus large gains on 01–07 and 09

record.verdict_notes: The safety direction is safe minus unsafe, the sign opposite to the refusal direction. Removing its projection from the modality shift is therefore a partial restoration toward the harmful side, not an ablation of refusal. Lower ASR is consistent with V1, so the reader's 'reversed' states were errors. ASR is a keyword-matching refusal proxy that includes broad words like 'However' and 'illegal', with no uncertainty reported. The intervention acts on last-token activations at selected layers. V2, V4-V8 are not tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not globally project the direction out at every layer and position, add it to induce refusals, or test safety-trained chat-only models. The intervention calibrates the projected component of the image-induced shift at selected layers in VLMs.
Measures the association between modality-induced shift alignment and attack success; does not directly suppress the direction as an attack intervention or train against its ablation.
Does not compare a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions.
Does not separate a harmfulness judgment representation from a refusal-decision representation.
No language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test of the direction.
Does not vary refusal-training methods or timing.

relationships.condition: VLMs (LLaVA-1.5/1.6, MiniGPT-4, ShareGPT4V, Qwen-VL): removing the safe-ward component along the diff-in-means direction
relationships.reason: Refusal rises: FigStep ASR drops to 6–9% (R16-R19), MM-SafetyBench ASR drops on all models (R01-R15). MME/MM-Vet utility is essentially unchanged (R20-R31).
relationships.display_finding: FigStep attack success fell to 6–9% and MM-SafetyBench attack success decreased across all tested models, while MME and MM-Vet utility remained essentially unchanged.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: VLMs (LLaVA-1.5/1.6, MiniGPT-4, ShareGPT4V, Qwen-VL): removing the safe-ward component along the diff-in-means direction
source_check.reason: Removing the projection moves activations back toward the harmful/refusal side, and ASR drops on every model and benchmark (e.g. FigStep 62.4->8.5). MME/MM-Vet scores barely change (Table 4). Only the addition/restoration half and the capability part of V1 are tested; ablation is untested. The row states 'reversed' on R01-R03, R16, R17 and R19 contradict this label and should be observed/partial.

relationships.condition: Choice of calibrated layer range, and MM-SafetyBench aggregate

relationships.display_finding: Calibration worked well only when starting in middle layers; all-layer or last-10-layer calibration left high ASR, and MM-SafetyBench ASR remained at 30–46%.

tranche.reason: New setting (VLMs) with its own results on the claim. Section 4 shows modality shifts align with the text-only diff-in-means safety direction, and this tracks jailbreak success. Removing that component restores refusal. This is more than reporting a method's performance, so not T4. The method differs from Arditi's global ablation and addition.

source_check.notes: ASR is scored by a broad rejection-keyword list (Table 11 includes 'However', 'avoid', 'illegal', 'responsible'), so refusals may be overcounted. The safety shift s is safe minus unsafe, the opposite sign to Arditi's direction. The layer range for the main results is not stated in the main text. Venue is not in the text: it is arXiv v1 (Feb 2025) in an ICML-style template, so the NeurIPS label comes only from metadata.

statements.correction: Subset-mean shift cosines with the safety shift (safe minus unsafe, text-only): success subset >0.7 (100% ASR by construction); failure subset <0.2 (0%); blank image positive. Figure 6 has LLaVA-1.5-7B and MiniGPT-4-7B panels. FigStep ASR Direct->ShiftDC: LLaVA-1.5-7B 62.4->8.5, ShareGPT4V-7B 28.7->9.2, MiniGPT-4-7B 12.5->6.3, Qwen-VL-7B 25.3->8.4. Capability check: MME/MM-Vet. No random-direction control.
statements.problem: Minor points. The >0.7/<0.2 values are cosines between the subset-mean modality shift and the text-only safety shift, not per-input alignment. The 100%/0% ASR hold by definition of the success/failure partition. The thresholds are given for Figure 6 as a whole, not per model. The 12.5->6.3 example is the smallest FigStep effect. The NeurIPS venue is not stated in this text (arXiv v1, Feb 2025).

statements.correction: Middle-layer probe accuracy: train and test on text-only ~90%; train and test on image-text ~65%; train on text and test on image-text ~60%. Of unsafe image-text inputs, ~70% are classed as safe. ShiftDC uses the text-only direction: e.g. LLaVA-1.5-7B MM-SafetyBench SD 45.4->38.0, OCR 69.3->39.7, FigStep 62.4->8.5.
statements.problem: Correct. The values hold at middle layers for both LLaVA-1.5-7B and MiniGPT-4-7B, with probes trained and tested within each modality. R01 is the weakest example of the anchor working.
